subject: tornado plot and line plot in 1 graph

messages.author: bd03678d4286b766
messages.subject: tornado plot and line plot in 1 graph
parts:
At the moment, I am conducting 2 Tornado diagrams (one population age pyramid
for displaying the European Standard population, the other one for the
German Population in 2011). To conduct these plots, I used the package
“plotrix” and the “pyramid.plot” syntax (please see the whole syntax for the
above described examples below).

It worked very well, but one problem remains. I have 2 population pyramids
in 2 different graphs. I would like to combine both plots in one graph in
order to demonstrate the differences between both populations, especially to
show that the German population has a higher percentage of older people. The
standard population reduces the percentage of the older population resulting
in biased incidence rates (when I compare raw incidence rates from Germany
with European-standardized incidence rates from Germany).

My goal would be to demonstrate the German age pyramid as a Tornado plot
usually used for age pyramids (as indicated in my syntax) and the age
distribution of the standard population in lines (to avoid the overlapping
of 2 tornado plots in 1 graph).


My question: Does anyone have any ideashow to perform a graph containing 2
different plots ( line plot and tornado plot).

Syntax for Tornado Plot using “plotrix” and “pyaramid.plot)

#.age pyramid (example "Europaeische Standardbevoelkerung")

library(plotrix)
xy.pop
<-c(8.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,6.0,5.0,4.0,3.0,2.0,1.0,1.0)
xx.pop
<-c(8.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,6.0,5.0,4.0,3.0,2.0,1.0,1.0)
agelabels <-c("0-4", "5-9","10-14","15-19", "20-24","25-29","30-34","35-39",
               "40-44", "45-49", "50-54","55-59", "60-64", "65-69", "70-74",
               "75-79", "80-84", "85+")
mcol <-color.gradient(c(0,0,0.5,1),c(0,0,0.5,1),c(1,1,0.5,1),18)
fcol <-color.gradient(c(1,1,0.5,1),c(0.5,0.5,0.5,1), c(0.5,0.5,0.5,1),18)
par(mar=pyramid.plot(xy.pop,xx.pop,labels=agelabels,
                      main="Europaeische Standardbevoelkerung",
                      lxcol=mcol,rxcol=fcol,gap=0.5,show.values=T))

#.age pyramid (example "Deutsche Bevoelkerung 2011")

library(plotrix)
xy.pop
<-c(4.3,4.5,5.0,5.2,6.3,6.3,6.2,6.0,8.1,9.1,8.1,6.9,6.0,4.8,5.8,3.7,2.3,1.4)
xx.pop
<-c(4.0,4.1,4.6,4.8,5.8,5.9,5.9,5.7,7.5,8.4,7.6,6.7,6.0,5.0,6.4,4.7,3.5,3.5)
agelabels <-c("0-4", "5-9","10-14","15-19", "20-24","25-29","30-34","35-39",
               "40-44", "45-49", "50-54","55-59", "60-64", "65-69", "70-74",
               "75-79", "80-84", "85+")
mcol <-color.gradient(c(0,0,0.5,1),c(0,0,0.5,1),c(1,1,0.5,1),18)
fcol <-color.gradient(c(1,1,0.5,1),c(0.5,0.5,0.5,1), c(0.5,0.5,0.5,1),18)
par(mar=pyramid.plot(xy.pop,xx.pop,labels=agelabels,
                      main="Deutsche Bevoelkerung 2011",
                      lxcol=mcol,rxcol=fcol,gap=0.5,show.values=T))
